reason: A corolla lip or lobe can be divided in two. The examples are correct.
An indusium (fern) can be glabrous.
Perianth lobes can be spreading.
A cypsela has a length. The examples are measurements.
A stipule margin can be fringed with hairs.
The indumentum has a colour (whitish, grayish).
A pinna can be pubescent.

Teeth can be lanceolate, but the examples (narrowly, broadly lanceolate) look like they describe the blade or the lobes. A rule would need to check that the shape word is attached to the tooth and not the leaf.
A pedicel can be lanate or woolly.
The examples are about a spur, which is the wrong part. A short shoot is not described as bent in these floras. The pair exists only through a wrong bearer reading.
An involucre can be floccose, often on its teeth.
A seed surface can be sculptured.
A leaflet can be setose.
An involucral bract can be dark. 'Dark' is a colour tone.
A mericarp can be cylindric, ovoid or ellipsoid. The PATO term is a generic parent shape, so a more specific shape term would be better where one exists.
An ochrea has a length. The examples are measurements.
Parallelodromous is the venation pattern of a whole leaf. 'Secondary veins parallel' says how the veins lie relative to each other, which is a different meaning.
'Capillary' means hair-thin, which is a thickness. It is not fibrillary (made of fibrils). The PATO term means something else.
A tepal can be winged.
A lemma apex can be entire.
A labellum lobe apex can be emarginate.
An anther cap has a shape (beaked, truncate-rounded, mucronate).
A lemma apex can be truncate.
A capitulum can be sessile or subsessile.
A flower has a colour. The PATO term is generic, so a more specific colour term is better where the data allows it.
A floral disc can be shorter than the ovary or sepals. This is a comparison with another part.
An ovary can be short or shorter than the calyx. Check that 'Pedicel and ovary' is split into two parts.
A seta can be elongate.
Tertiary veins can be conspicuous or distinct.
The examples (mentum, spur, 'longer than ovary') describe other parts. A short shoot is the wrong bearer here.
Alar cells (mosses) can be quadrate.
The text says ellipsoidal, which is the PATO ellipsoid. Prolate is a different, narrower term, so this is the wrong reading.
A domatium can be pubescent. The examples are French and are correct.
'Appendices subglobuleux' describes appendages. The banner petal is the wrong bearer, so the pair exists only through a wrong part reading.
'Canaliculé' usually describes the whole blade or petiole, but some examples say 'towards base'. A rule would need to know whether the groove belongs to the base or to the whole organ.
A fruit has a length-to-width ratio.
A spadix or its zone can be cylindric.
'Angled' (an angle at the base or side) is not 'bent'. The PATO term means something else.
A pappus can be ciliate.
'Characteristic' is too generic. 'Simple or forked' is a branching type. A rule or a specific trichome-type term is needed.
A perigynium (beak margin) can be entire.
A leaflet can be scaly or lepidote.
A petal has a colour. The PATO term is generic, so a more specific colour term is better where possible.
A pappus can have stout or thickened bristles.
Inflorescence branches can be hairy.
A pedicel can be dilated at its tip.
Teeth can be glandular.
A count of bracteoles can be few. The examples are correct.

The examples describe the lamina (ligule) shape, and one example is 'drooping or arching', which is a posture. A rule would need to map ligule or lamina to its own part and send posture words elsewhere.
A leaf apex can be subulate.
Leaflets can overlap.
A spathe can be deciduous. The 'caducous' example is a close synonym.
A leaf blade can be dark. 'Dark' is a colour tone.
A secretory tissue portion (gland, resin spot) has a diameter.
A stipe or stalk can be dark.
An orchid labellum can be convex. Some examples are about the midvein or an outer face, so check that the part is right.
'Uniseriate' is a cell arrangement (one row of cells) and not a spatial pattern in the PATO sense. A rule would need a separate seriate or cell-row term.
Leaf cells can be obscure or indistinct.
A leaf rachis can bear prickles, so it can be spiny.
A corolla tube can be funnel-shaped. The French examples are correct.
